limitations: P1 — Positive Gaussian operator contradicts negative-coefficient selection — Counterevidence: Release uses gaus1 derivative, which allows signed coefficients; likely operator specification difference

P1 — Positive Gaussian operator contradicts negative-coefficient selection — Alternative readings and counterevidence: Static reinspection of both released converters confirms wavename="gaus1" and arange(1,4). Independently consulted official PyWavelets CWT documentation, Gaussian Derivative Wavelets section (https://pywavelets.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ref/cwt.html#gaussian-derivative-wavelets), on 2026-10-25: gausP is a derivative of a normalized Gaussian. Its first derivative changes sign, removing the positivity argument for the released alternate kernel. N-CAR uses <0 whereas N_Caltech101 uses !=0, so even those two selection rules differ. The text or notation may have omitted an intended derivative; that is plausible but is not the printed operator.

P2 — Periodic-input chaos derivation has invalid recurrence and fixed-point steps — Counterevidence: Selected code parameters differ and may have other dynamics; no proof of universal absence of chaos

P2 — Periodic-input chaos derivation has invalid recurrence and fixed-point steps — Alternative readings and counterevidence: The release uses alpha_f=.1, alpha_e=1, VE=50, outside the counterexample. Neither that regime nor universal nonexistence of chaos was proved. Figures showing irregular waveforms and finite phase portraits are not mathematical chaos certification; a narrower empirical parameter-specific reading can survive the counterexample but is unsupported by the printed recurrence/equilibrium proof.
